relevance_note: 1972 biochemical study of HDL in named Tangier patients: "Seven patients homozygous for Tangier disease (Pe. Lo., Pa. Lo., T. La., E. La., J. Mi., C. Mi., and C. No.)" and two sets of heterozygous parents.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand (OCR text with garbled passages); a short script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. In scope: 7 homozygous Tangier patients and 4 heterozygous parents, all labelled by the paper's own initials. The paper does not say which parents belong to which patients, so no family labels or relation labels were assigned. No gene or variant is named (pre-molecular era; the authors hypothesise an apoLp-Gln-I regulatory mutation), so the variants table is empty; 'homozygous'/'heterozygous' refer to the disease trait, not a printed ABCA1 variant. is_proband left null (no one called proband). Publication year is not printed in the text (only received/revised dates), so year is null. Group statements: the Results' first paragraph names 'the seven patients homozygous for Tangier disease', used for low HDL cholesterol/no alpha band/HDLr; Table V and gel results name four patients (Pe. Lo., Pa. Lo., T. La., E. La.) for decreased apoLp-Gln-I (apoA-I per the nomenclature table). Table IV is patients-as-columns; column header 'Concentration in d 1.063- 1.2 10 fractioi of Tangier patient (Pa. Lo.)'. Heterozygotes' HDL cholesterol 22-30 mg/100 ml is a group range; the paper does not call it low, so the checklist item is not reported for them. Pe. Lo.'s transiently normal HDL (36 mg/100 ml) right after bypass reflects transfusion of normal blood and was not recorded as an exclusion. Pe. Lo.'s fever was postoperative. Not extracted: single patients from Britain, Germany and New Zealand mentioned in passing in the Discussion (only country and HDLr presence given); 10 liver-disease patients, hyperlipoproteinemia patients and >300 normal controls (out of scope; no total cohort size stated). No contradictions found.
